title: The failed attack on Jerusalem
summary: Rezin, king of Syria, and Pekah, son of Remaliah, go up to war against Jerusalem but cannot prevail.

explicit_facts.text: Rezin, king of Syria, and Pekah son of Remaliah went up toward Jerusalem to war against it but could not prevail.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The two kings and their forces approach Jerusalem in a military campaign.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance and number of soldiers, weapons, clothing, architecture, and outcome of the campaign beyond failure to prevail.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show Jerusalem being captured or a battle outcome not stated.

title: Fear in the house of David
summary: The house of David is told Syria is allied with Ephraim; the king and his people are shaken with fear.

explicit_facts.text: The house of David is told that Syria is confederate with Ephraim.
The heart of the king and his people is moved like trees moved by wind.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The people appear alarmed upon hearing the report.
unspecified_visual_details: The messenger's identity, the precise hearers, and their appearance.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The trees moved by wind are a figure of speech for fear, not a literal event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict literal trees or wind as the cause of the people's reaction.

title: Isaiah is sent to meet Ahaz
summary: The Lord tells Isaiah to go with his son Shearjashub to meet Ahaz at the end of the conduit of the upper pool.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord tells Isaiah to go with Shearjashub to meet Ahaz at the end of the conduit of the upper pool in the highway of the fuller's field.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Isaiah and Shearjashub meet Ahaz at the specified water conduit.
unspecified_visual_details: Whether Ahaz is already there when Isaiah and his son arrive; the appearance of the conduit and surrounding area.

spoken_dialogue.text: Go forth now to meet Ahaz, thou and Shearjashub thy son, at the end of the conduit of the upper pool in the highway of the fuller’s field;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord visibly; no appearance is described.

title: Isaiah reassures Ahaz
summary: Isaiah delivers the Lord's warning to Ahaz not to fear Rezin and the son of Remaliah.

explicit_facts.text: Isaiah is instructed to tell Ahaz to take heed, be quiet, and not fear or be faint-hearted over Rezin and the son of Remaliah.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Isaiah speaks to Ahaz at their meeting place.
unspecified_visual_details: Ahaz's response and the visible appearance of the two kings.

spoken_dialogue.text: Take heed, and be quiet; fear not, neither be faint-hearted
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Isaiah

spoken_dialogue.text: for the two tails of these smoking firebrands
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Isaiah

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The smoking firebrands are a figure of speech, not literal objects.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Rezin or Pekah as present.

title: The plot against Judah
summary: Isaiah recounts the evil counsel of Syria, Ephraim, and the son of Remaliah to attack Judah and install the son of Tabeal as king.

explicit_facts.text: Syria, Ephraim, and the son of Remaliah have taken counsel against Ahaz.
Their plan is to go against Judah, breach it, and set the son of Tabeal as king there.

unspecified_visual_details: The participants in the reported counsel and where it took place.

spoken_dialogue.text: Let us go up against Judah and vex it, and let us make a breach therein for us, and set a king in the midst of it, yea, the son of Tabeal.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Reported conspirators

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The plan is reported speech, not a present-tense meeting of the conspirators.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show the conspirators physically meeting or carrying out the plot.

title: The plot will fail
summary: The Lord declares the plan will not stand and warns that Ephraim will cease to be a people; Ahaz must believe to be established.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord declares that the plot will not stand or come to pass.
The Lord says Ephraim will be broken within sixty-five years so that it will not be a people.
Ahaz is warned that unless he believes, he will not be established.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Isaiah speaks the Lord's message to Ahaz.
unspecified_visual_details: Any visual representation of the future breaking of Ephraim.

spoken_dialogue.text: It shall not stand, neither shall it come to pass.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Isaiah

spoken_dialogue.text: If ye will not believe surely ye shall not be established.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Isaiah

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The prophecy is spoken, not depicted as a separate future event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not create a visual scene of Ephraim's future destruction.

title: The Lord offers Ahaz a sign
summary: The Lord tells Ahaz to ask for a sign, but Ahaz refuses to ask or tempt the Lord.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord speaks again to Ahaz and tells him to ask for a sign in the depths or heights above.
Ahaz refuses to ask, saying he will not tempt the Lord.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Ahaz hears the Lord's words and answers.
unspecified_visual_details: The Lord's visible appearance and Ahaz's precise setting.

spoken_dialogue.text: Ask thee a sign of the Lord thy God; ask it either in the depths, or in the heights above.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: I will not ask, neither will I tempt the Lord.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Ahaz

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a visible divine figure or a sign; neither is described as visibly appearing.

title: The sign of Immanuel
summary: The Lord declares a sign: a virgin will conceive and bear a son named Immanuel, who will eat butter and honey.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord addresses the house of David and says a virgin shall conceive and bear a son named Immanuel.
The child shall eat butter and honey.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The message is delivered to Ahaz.
unspecified_visual_details: The identity and appearance of the virgin and child, and when or where the prophesied birth takes place.

spoken_dialogue.text: Hear ye now, O house of David; is it a small thing for you to weary men, but will ye weary my God also?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Isaiah

spoken_dialogue.text: Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and shall bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Isaiah

spoken_dialogue.text: Butter and honey shall he eat,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Isaiah

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The future birth is spoken as prophecy; do not stage it as a present event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the virgin's or child's identity, appearance, or birthplace.

title: The land forsaken by its kings
summary: Before the child can choose good and refuse evil, the land Ahaz abhors will be forsaken by both its kings; the Lord will bring days of affliction through the king of Assyria.

explicit_facts.text: Before the child knows to refuse evil and choose good, the land Ahaz abhors will be forsaken by both its kings.
The Lord shall bring upon Ahaz, his people, and his father's house days unlike those since Ephraim departed from Judah, through the king of Assyria.

unspecified_visual_details: The future events involving the kings and Assyria.

spoken_dialogue.text: For before the child shall know to refuse the evil and choose the good, the land that thou abhorrest shall be forsaken of both her kings.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Isaiah

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are future events reported in prophecy, not a present visual scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage an Assyrian invasion or kings abandoning the land.

title: The fly and the bee
summary: The Lord will summon the fly from Egypt and the bee from Assyria; they will settle in desolate valleys, rock holes, thorns, and bushes.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord shall hiss for the fly in Egypt and the bee in Assyria.
They shall come and rest in desolate valleys, holes of rocks, thorns, and bushes.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The fly and bee may be shown among the listed desolate terrain.
unspecified_visual_details: Whether the fly and bee are literal insects or figures of speech; their number and appearance.

narration.text: And it shall come to pass in that day

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The fly and bee may signify forces from Egypt and Assyria; do not portray them as armies without explicit support.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict human armies or a divine figure.

title: The hired razor
summary: The Lord's message compares Assyria's action to a hired razor shaving the head, hair of the feet, and beard.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord shall shave with a hired razor by the king of Assyria the head and hair of the feet, and it shall consume the beard.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The razor is a metaphor for the king of Assyria's action.
unspecified_visual_details: The identity of the person being shaved and the historical event represented.

narration.text: the Lord shave with a razor that is hired

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The shaving imagery is figurative; the source does not narrate a literal shaving.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show a person being shaved or identify a specific victim.

title: A man with livestock
summary: In that day a man will tend a young cow and two sheep; those left in the land will eat butter and honey.

explicit_facts.text: A man shall nourish a young cow and two sheep.
Those left in the land shall eat butter and honey.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The man tends the young cow and two sheep.
unspecified_visual_details: The man's identity, appearance, and exact location; the number and identities of those left in the land.

narration.text: for the abundance of milk they shall give he shall eat butter

prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the man or invent a household or community.

title: Vineyards become overgrown
summary: Places once containing valuable vineyards will become briers and thorns; men will come there with bows and arrows because of the overgrowth.

explicit_facts.text: Places that had a thousand vines valued at a thousand silverlings shall become briers and thorns.
Men shall come there with arrows and bows because the land will become briers and thorns.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Men carry bows and arrows into thorn-covered former vineyard land.
unspecified_visual_details: The men's identities, clothing, number, and purpose beyond coming because of the overgrowth.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse does not say that the men are hunting or fighting.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict battle, a specific conflict, or a named group.

title: Hills for grazing
summary: Hills once dug with a mattock will no longer be feared for briers and thorns, but will be used by oxen and lesser cattle.

explicit_facts.text: Hills dug with a mattock will be used for sending forth oxen and the treading of lesser cattle, without fear of briers and thorns.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Oxen and lesser cattle graze or tread on the hills.
unspecified_visual_details: The hills' exact appearance, the number of animals, and whether a herder is present.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a future condition described by prophecy.
prohibited_inventions: Do not add a herder or depict an unstated cause for the land's condition.
